 Order 
This writ petition has been filed this writ petition challenging the impugned orders in R.No.3055/2024/S12/FSD, dated 29.06.2024 and in R.No.3055/2024/S12/FSD, dated 29.06.2024 on the file of the first respondent with a consequential direction to the respondents to permit the petitioner to retire with all service and monetary benefits within the time stipulated by this Court.
2. Heard Mr.S.Louis, learned counsel for the petitioner, Mr.J.Ashok, learned Additional Government Pleader for the respondents. By consent of both parties, this writ petition is taken up for final disposal at the stage of admission itself. 
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 3. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner was working as the Food Safety Officer at Palayamkottai Zone, Tirunelveli Corporation and a criminal case came to be registered against the petitioner and his wife in Crime No.12 of 2023 on the false allegation. He has been placed under suspension at the verge of his retirement ie., 29.06.2024 and he was also not allowed to retire on the date of superannuation ie., on 30.06.2024.
4. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner further submitted that the Government, in G.O.Ms.No.111, Human Resources Management (N) Department, dated 11.10.2021, has held that the government servants should not be placed under suspension on the last date of his service. Even though a case has been registered in the year 2023 itself, there was no progress till the date of the superannuation and therefore, placing a government servant under suspension on the last date of his superannuation is unsustainable and so, he prays this Court to set aside the impugned orders and allow him to retire subject to the result of the criminal case.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 5. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner also drew the attention of this Court to the guidelines for avoiding suspension on the last date of his retirement issued in the Government Order in G.O.(Ms) No. 111, Human Resource Management (N) Department, dated 11.10.2021. The Government has reiterated the guidelines already issued in G.O.Ms.No.144, Personnel and Administrative Reforms (N) Department, dated 08.06.2007, to avoid last minute suspension. 
6. The learned Additional Government Pleader appearing for the respondents submitted that the respondents were not aware of the case registered against the petitioner and only after getting the A.R.Sankaralingam vs The Commissioner Of Food Safety And Drug ... on 4 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67420780/
2 report of the Vigilance and Anti Corruption dated 10.05.2024, they came to know about that a case has been registered against the petitioner as early as in the year 2023 in Crime No.12 of 2023 and that the investigation is pending. The gravity of the allegations are very serious in nature and therefore, the respondents thought it fit to keep the petitioner under suspension before his retirement. Even though the general rule states that https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis the government servant shall not be placed under suspension at the verge of his retirement, when serious allegations involving in corrupt activities are concerned, such employees cannot expect liberal permission for retirement. 
7. On perusal of the impugned order, it is seen that a regular case has been registered against the petitioner on the allegation of possession of disproportionate assets to the tune of Rs.49,68,251/-
during the check period from 01.04.2003 to 31.03.2015. It is also stated that the investigation of Vigilance and Anti Corruption is in progress. 
8. Till the petitioner was in service, no departmental action has been initiated against the petitioner on the complaint which was made before the Vigilance and Anti Corruption. Even at the time when the petitioner was served with the order of suspension, he was not given with any charge memo. In that view of the matter, the petitioner may be allowed to retire subject to pending criminal case, by setting aside the impugned order. 
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 9 . Accordingly, this Writ Petition is allowed and the impugned orders dated 29.06.2024 are set aside and the petitioner is allowed to retire subject to the result of the criminal case. No costs. 
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petition is closed.
